newsitem.title: UK: BA little changed after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: BA little changed after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc were little moved in early trading on Tuesday after first-half results in line with market expectations.
The stock was down 1/2p at 549 by 0810 GMT.
The airline posted a 9.3 percent rise in first-half pre-tax profit to 470 million stg, compared with analyst expectations mostly in a range between 449 milion stg and 480 million.
Its dividend rose to 4.25p per share from 3.85p, compared with expectations ranging from 4.2p to 4.5p.

"Profits are basically in line and the dividend is bang in line so there are no shocks there," said Selwyn Jones, analyst at Credit Lyonnais Laing. "I see no reason to change our forecasts or our hold recommendation."
Analysts said the underlying result had been constrained by rising fuel costs, and although this was expected the issue was likely to continue in the short term.
"The result is pretty much as expected with operating profit down and growth driven by non-operating items," said Guy Kekwick, analyst at Lehman Brothers.
"I don't think the issue of rising fuel costs will go away as we go into the fourth quarter."
BA also said its scheduled passenger yield rose 4.1 percent to 6.54p in the period while October passenger traffic was up 6.5 percent.
Chairman Sir Colin Marshall said: "The economic outlook for the main countries in which we operate remains generally encouraging with forecasts of continued steady growth in supply and demand."
On the proposed alliance with American Airlines, he said the government approval process was taking longer than expected but "we remain optimistic that matters will be resolved satisfactorily."
